intent.raw_query: Hawaii family beach vacation, $5000, 10 days, August 2026 from Seattle

selected_hotel.name: Hanauma Bay, East Oahu Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay
experiences.description: Explore one of Hawaii's most pristine marine sanctuaries with the whole family. Hanauma Bay offers calm, clear waters teeming with colorful tropical fish and sea turtles, making it perfect for beginner and experienced snorkelers alike. Equipment rentals are available on-site and an educational center teaches visitors about the reef ecosystem before entering the water.

experiences.name: Luau Dinner at Old Lahaina Luau
experiences.description: Immerse your family in authentic Hawaiian culture with a traditional luau featuring a feast of kalua pig, poi, lomi salmon, and haupia dessert. Enjoy live music, hula dancing performances, and fire knife dancing under the stars along the oceanfront. This is a memorable cultural dining experience that kids and adults will talk about for years.

experiences.name: Polynesian Cultural Center Day Trip
experiences.description: Spend a full day exploring six authentic Polynesian village recreations representing Hawaii, Samoa, Aotearoa, Fiji, Tahiti, and Tonga. Families can participate in hands-on cultural activities like spear throwing, coconut husking, and traditional weaving. The evening features an all-you-can-eat buffet and a spectacular live show called 'Ha: Breath of Life'.

experiences.name: Surfing Lessons at Waikiki Beach
experiences.description: Take beginner surfing lessons with certified instructors on the gentle, rolling waves of Waikiki, considered one of the best places in the world to learn to surf. Group lessons are available for all ages including young children, and most participants are standing on the board within the first session. A quintessential Hawaiian family activity with iconic Diamond Head views in the background.

experiences.name: Road to Hana Scenic Drive and Waterfalls
experiences.description: Embark on one of the most scenic drives in the world along Maui's northeastern coastline, stopping at lush rainforest waterfalls, black sand beaches, and bamboo forests. Family highlights include swimming at Wailua Falls, exploring the Pools of Oheo, and tasting fresh banana bread from roadside stands. Pack a picnic and make a full day of this breathtaking adventure through tropical paradise.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Hawaii
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Hanauma Bay, East Oahu Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 — skip morning activities. After landing, collect luggage, pick up a rental car or take TheBus (Route 23) to save money, and head to your Hanauma Bay, East Oahu boutique stay to check in.
day_by_day.afternoon: Once settled, take a short walk to nearby Sandy Beach Park (free entry, just 5 minutes from Hanauma Bay area) to dip your toes in the Pacific, shake off jet lag, and soak in your first Hawaiian sunset views. Pick up snacks and groceries at the nearby Foodland Farms in Hawaii Kai to stock your room and save on meals throughout the trip.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed first evening at the Koko Marina Center in Hawaii Kai — browse the waterfront shops and grab an affordable dinner at one of the casual eateries nearby.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a snack at the airport
meals.lunch: Pick up a plate lunch from a food truck or L&L Hawaiian Barbecue near the airport (~$10–$12)
meals.dinner: Koko Marina Center — try Zippy's for local comfort food (chili rice, saimin) for under $15 per person

day_by_day.notes: Buy a reusable water bottle and sunscreen at Foodland Farms tonight — both are essential and cheaper bought locally than at tourist shops. TheBus day pass is $7.50/person if you skip the rental car.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve — one of Hawaii's best snorkeling spots and it's right at your doorstep! Arrive early (opens 6:45 AM) to beat crowds. Entry is $25/adult, free for children under 13. Rent snorkel gear on-site (~$15) or bring your own. Watch the free marine education video before entering the bay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or drive to Koko Head Crater Trail — a challenging but rewarding hike up 1,048 railway tie steps with panoramic views of East Oahu. Free to hike. Bring plenty of water. After the hike, cool off at Halona Blowhole Lookout (free, 5-minute drive) and watch the ocean spray through the lava rock.
day_by_day.evening: Drive to Makapu'u Point Lighthouse Trail for a golden-hour sunset walk (free, paved trail, 2 miles round trip, family-friendly). Watch for spinner dolphins and humpback whales in season from the lookout.

meals.breakfast: Prepare a simple breakfast from your Foodland groceries — cereal, fruit, yogurt (~$3–$5 per person)
meals.lunch: Pack sandwiches and snacks from your room to eat at Hanauma Bay picnic area (save $15+ per person)
meals.dinner: Ono Seafood in Kaimuki (~20 min drive) — famous local poke bowls for $12–$16. Cash preferred.

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay reservations are required in advance at dlnr.hawaii.gov/hanauma — book online before your trip. Monday availability is generally better than weekends. Parking is $3.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Diamond Head State Monument (~25 min from your hotel). Hike the iconic 1.6-mile round-trip trail inside the volcanic crater for stunning views of Waikiki and the Pacific. Entry is $5/person or $10/car. Arrive by 8 AM to avoid midday heat and crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Waikiki Beach (free) — swim, build sandcastles, and enjoy the lively beach atmosphere. Kids can try a beginner surf lesson at one of the budget-friendly beach concessions (~$25–$35/person for group lessons). Walk the Waikiki strip and visit the free Kuhio Beach Hula Show area.
day_by_day.evening: Catch the FREE Kuhio Beach Torch Lighting & Hula Show at Kuhio Beach Park (Tuesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday at sunset). A wonderful cultural experience for the whole family.

meals.breakfast: Grab malasadas (Portuguese donuts) from Leonard's Bakery on the way (~$1.50 each) — a must-try Hawaii treat
meals.lunch: Rainbow Drive-In in Kapahulu — iconic local plate lunch spot, $9–$13 per plate. Try the loco moco!
meals.dinner: Waikiki Beach Walk food court or Marugame Udon for fresh udon noodles under $12 per person

day_by_day.notes: Parking in Waikiki is expensive ($3–$5/hour). Consider taking TheBus Route 23 from Hawaii Kai directly to Waikiki to save money. The hula show is a highlight for families — bring a blanket to sit on the grass.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Chinatown Honolulu — a vibrant, budget-friendly neighborhood with colorful markets, art galleries, and cultural history. Visit the Oahu Market (fresh tropical fruits, local snacks), browse the lei stands on Maunakea Street, and explore the historic Chinatown Cultural Plaza. Free to explore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the Hawaii State Capitol and Iolani Palace (~10 min from Chinatown). Tour the grounds for free or take a guided tour of Iolani Palace — the only royal palace on US soil — for $25/adult, $6/child (ages 5–12). Then stroll through the nearby King Kamehameha Statue for photos.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Bishop Museum in the late afternoon (open until 5 PM) — Hawaii's premier natural history museum. Admission is $25/adult, $17/child. Explore Hawaiian artifacts, the planetarium, and interactive family exhibits.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast from your hotel room supplies or grab fresh fruit and a snack from Chinatown Market (~$3–$5)
meals.lunch: Eat in Chinatown — try Fook Yuen for dim sum or a local Vietnamese pho shop for $8–$12 per person
meals.dinner: Cook a simple dinner at your accommodation using groceries from Foodland to save money after a spending day

day_by_day.notes: Chinatown is most lively in the morning — aim to arrive by 9 AM. The area is safe during the day but stay aware of your surroundings in the evening. Iolani Palace tours must be reserved in advance at iolanipalace.org.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to the North Shore (~45–60 min from your hotel) and visit Waimea Valley — a beautiful botanical garden and nature park with a waterfall swimming hole at the end. Entry is $20/adult, $10/child. The 1.5-mile walk through lush gardens is perfect for families. Swim at the waterfall pool (life jackets provided).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue along the North Shore to Sunset Beach and Ehukai Beach Park (Banzai Pipeline). In summer, the waves are calm and perfect for swimming and snorkeling (free). Walk the shoreline, explore tide pools, and grab shave ice from a roadside stand. Stop at Shark's Cove in Pupukea for excellent snorkeling (free).
day_by_day.evening: Drive back via the Kamehameha Highway and stop at the famous Giovanni's Shrimp Truck in Kahuku for dinner — a legendary North Shore institution.

meals.breakfast: Pack breakfast from your room to eat on the road or at Waimea Valley picnic tables
meals.lunch: Matsumoto Shave Ice in Haleiwa town — iconic Hawaiian treat ($4–$6). Grab plate lunch from a nearby food truck ($10–$13)
meals.dinner: Giovanni's Shrimp Truck — scampi or spicy shrimp plate with rice for $16–$18 per plate (worth every penny!)

day_by_day.notes: The North Shore drive is beautiful — leave by 8 AM to make the most of the day. Gas up your car before heading out as stations are sparse on the North Shore. Summer months mean calm waters ideal for families.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Pearl Harbor National Memorial — one of Hawaii's most significant historical sites. The USS Arizona Memorial (boat tour) is FREE but requires timed-entry passes reserved in advance at recreation.gov. The visitor center and exhibits are also free. Plan to spend 2–3 hours here.
day_by_day.afternoon: If budget allows, add the USS Missouri Battleship tour ($34/adult, $17/child) or USS Bowfin Submarine Museum ($17/adult, $9/child) for a fuller Pearl Harbor experience. Alternatively, visit the free Pacific Aviation Museum Pearl Harbor exhibits from the outside or head to nearby Aloha Stadium Swap Meet (Wednesday, Saturday, Sunday) — check if it falls on your schedule.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the East Oahu area and enjoy a relaxing evening at Maunalua Bay Beach Park near your hotel — a calm, family-friendly beach perfect for kayaking or stand-up paddleboarding rentals (~$15–$20/hour).

meals.breakfast: Home-prepared breakfast from your room supplies
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch to eat at Pearl Harbor picnic areas — no outside food in the memorial itself, but picnic areas are nearby
meals.dinner: Kona Brewing Company at Koko Marina Center — burgers and local craft beer in a family-friendly setting. Budget ~$15–$20/person for food

day_by_day.notes: Pearl Harbor USS Arizona Memorial passes sell out weeks in advance — book before your trip at recreation.gov. Bags are not allowed inside the memorial; free storage lockers are available. Allow extra time for security screening.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the KCC Farmers Market at Kapiolani Community College (open Saturdays 7:30 AM–11 AM, free entry). Browse local produce, taste free samples, buy affordable fresh fruit, local honey, and Hawaiian coffee. One of Oahu's best free experiences. Combine with a walk through the adjacent Kapiolani Park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at Ala Moana Beach Park — a long, reef-protected beach that's calmer and less crowded than Waikiki, perfect for families with young children. Free parking and entry. Afterward, browse Ala Moana Center (the largest open-air shopping mall in the US) — even window shopping is fun and free!
day_by_day.evening: Head to Magic Island (Aina Moana State Recreation Area) adjacent to Ala Moana Beach for a beautiful sunset view over the Honolulu skyline and Diamond Head. A perfect, free family moment.

meals.breakfast: Fresh fruit, pastries, and local snacks from the KCC Farmers Market (~$5–$10 per person)
meals.lunch: Food trucks near Ala Moana Beach Park or grab groceries from the Foodland in Ala Moana Center for a beach picnic
meals.dinner: Side Street Inn on Hopaka — a beloved local restaurant with generous portions. Try the pan-fried pork chops. Budget ~$15–$20/person

day_by_day.notes: The KCC Farmers Market is cash-preferred. Bring a reusable bag for produce. Ala Moana Beach Park has free parking, restrooms, and showers — great for a full family beach day. Arrive at Magic Island 30 minutes before sunset for the best spot.

day_by_day.morning: Take a scenic drive along the Windward Coast — head over the Pali Highway (stop at Nu'uanu Pali Lookout for breathtaking views, $7 parking fee) and down to Kailua town. Visit Kailua Beach Park — consistently rated one of the best beaches in the US. Calm turquoise water perfect for families. Free entry.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent kayaks or stand-up paddleboards in Kailua (~$25–$40/hour for a double kayak) and paddle to the Mokulua Islands just offshore — a stunning adventure. Alternatively, explore the charming Kailua town shops and galleries on foot. Drive to nearby Lanikai Beach for a short walk to the Lanikai Pillboxes hike (free, 1 mile round trip, great views).
day_by_day.evening: Drive back over the Pali Highway at dusk for atmospheric mountain views, then enjoy a quiet evening near your hotel.

meals.breakfast: Home-prepared breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Kailua town has great budget options — try Kalapawai Market for sandwiches and local deli items (~$10–$14)
meals.dinner: Boots & Kimo's Homestyle Kitchen in Kailua (famous for macadamia nut pancakes at dinner too!) — budget ~$12–$18/person. Arrive early as lines form quickly.

day_by_day.notes: Kailua Beach has free parking but it fills up fast on Sundays — arrive by 9 AM. The Lanikai Pillboxes hike is short but steep; wear proper shoes and bring water. The Pali Highway lookout can be windy — hold onto hats and small children!

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Manoa Falls Trail — a beautiful, easy 1.6-mile round-trip hike through a lush rainforest leading to a stunning 150-foot waterfall. Located just above Honolulu. Parking is $5. Trail is free. Wear water shoes as the trail can be muddy. Perfect for families.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Lyon Arboretum near the trailhead — a stunning 200-acre botanical garden with free admission (donations welcome). Explore rare Hawaiian plants, tropical flowers, and peaceful garden paths. Then drive to the University of Hawaii at Manoa campus for a free self-guided walk — beautiful architecture and a lively atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Spend your second-to-last evening revisiting your favorite beach near the hotel — Hanauma Bay area or Sandy Beach — for a sunset swim and reflection on the trip.

meals.breakfast: Grab coffee and pastries from Morning Glass Coffee in Manoa (~$5–$8) — a beloved local café near the trailhead
meals.lunch: Andy's Sandwiches & Smoothies near Manoa — local institution with fresh sandwiches and fruit smoothies for $8–$12
meals.dinner: Sorabol Korean Restaurant in Honolulu — all-you-can-eat Korean BBQ for ~$25/person, a fun and filling family dinner experience

day_by_day.notes: The Manoa Falls Trail can be slippery after rain — check conditions beforehand. Mosquito repellent is strongly recommended for the rainforest trail. The Lyon Arboretum is a hidden gem that most tourists skip — don't miss it!

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — wake up early for one last sunrise at Hanauma Bay overlook (free viewpoint from the parking area above the bay). Take a slow, nostalgic walk along the nearby coastline. Pack your bags and check out of your boutique stay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, squeeze in a quick stop at Kahala Mall for last-minute souvenir shopping (more affordable than Waikiki tourist shops). Pick up local treats like Honolulu Cookie Company cookies, Hawaiian Host macadamia chocolates, or Kona coffee as gifts. Head to the airport with plenty of time — allow 2–3 hours before departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — carry the aloha spirit home! Review your trip highlights and start planning your return.

meals.breakfast: Final home-cooked breakfast from remaining groceries or a last malasada from Leonard's Bakery if passing by
meals.lunch: Grab a plate lunch from a nearby food truck or L&L Hawaiian Barbecue near the airport for a final local meal (~$10–$13)
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Use up any remaining cash on local snacks and souvenirs — coins and small bills won't be useful back home. Return your rental car with a full tank (gas near the airport is cheaper than the rental company's refueling fee). Mahalo for an amazing Hawaii adventure!

trip_options.title: Classic Hawaii Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Flight LH lands; clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange ground transportation to Hanauma Bay, East Oahu Boutique Stay (~30–45 min drive from HNL).
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to the boutique stay, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll along the shoreline near Hanauma Bay to get oriented. Enjoy the views and let the kids splash in the shallows at a nearby beach access point.
day_by_day.evening: Welcome dinner at a nearby casual restaurant in the East Oahu area — try Kona Brewing Company (Hawaii Kai) for family-friendly atmosphere, local craft beers for adults, and hearty plates like fish tacos and burgers at mid-range prices (~$20–35/person).

meals.breakfast: Onboard flight or airport snack upon arrival
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the airport or a nearby deli/café en route to the hotel (Island Brew Coffeehouse at HNL is a solid option)
meals.dinner: Kona Brewing Company – Hawaii Kai (~$20–35/person, family-friendly, local craft beers and pub fare)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light to combat jet lag. Pick up a snorkel gear rental reservation for Hanauma Bay (Day 2) — reservations are mandatory and must be made online in advance at the Hawaii DLNR portal. Also confirm luau booking if not yet done.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay — arrive early (gates open at 6:45 AM; entry is timed/reserved). Watch the mandatory 9-minute marine education video, then spend 2–3 hours snorkeling the stunning reef. Spot sea turtles, parrotfish, and hundreds of tropical species in crystal-clear water. Perfect for all ages.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel for a midday rest and lunch. Afterward, visit nearby Makapu'u Lookout (~10 min drive) for breathtaking coastal views and a short, paved 2-mile round-trip hike suitable for families. Look for humpback whales (seasonal) and enjoy panoramic ocean vistas.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Ono Seafood or Roy's Hawaii Kai — Roy's offers a polished mid-range dining experience with Hawaiian fusion cuisine perfect for a special second-night treat (~$35–55/person). Alternatively, Ono Seafood is a beloved local poke spot for a budget-friendly, authentic experience (~$10–15/person).

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the boutique stay or a nearby café such as Kaimana Farm Café (fresh local fruit, acai bowls, eggs)
meals.lunch: Packed snacks/sandwiches from a local grocery (Times Supermarket, Hawaii Kai) eaten at the beach or hotel
meals.dinner: Roy's Hawaii Kai for Hawaiian fusion (~$35–55/person) or Ono Seafood for poke bowls (~$10–15/person)

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay requires advance online reservations — confirm the night before. Apply reef-safe sunscreen only (required by law). Bring water shoes for kids. Parking is limited; arrive right at opening time.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Waikiki (~25 min from Hanauma Bay) for Surfing Lessons at Waikiki Beach. Book a 2-hour group lesson with a certified instructor through Hans Hedemann Surf School or Waikiki Beach Services. The gentle, rolling waves of Waikiki are ideal for beginners and kids ages 5+. Everyone in the family can participate.
day_by_day.afternoon: After lessons, enjoy free time on Waikiki Beach — build sandcastles, swim, or rent a catamaran for a short sail. Walk along Kalakaua Avenue and browse the International Market Place for souvenirs and local crafts. Stop for shave ice at Waiola Shave Ice, a local institution.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner on Waikiki strip — Marukame Udon is a beloved, affordable spot with handmade udon noodles and tempura (~$8–12/person, expect a short queue). For a slightly elevated experience, try the Shore Bird at Outrigger Reef for open-air grilling right on the beach (~$25–40/person).

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the boutique stay or grab açaí bowls and smoothies from Bogart's Café near Diamond Head en route to Waikiki
meals.lunch: Shave ice and light snacks on the beach; grab plate lunches from a Waikiki food truck or Rainbow Drive-In (~$10–15/person)
meals.dinner: Marukame Udon (~$8–12/person) or Shore Bird at Outrigger Reef (~$25–40/person)

day_by_day.notes: Book surf lessons at least 2–3 days in advance. Apply reef-safe sunscreen. Bring a change of clothes and a bag for wet gear. Waikiki parking can be expensive — use TheBus or rideshare from East Oahu to save money.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day trip to the Polynesian Cultural Center (PCC) on Oahu's North Shore (~45 min drive from Hanauma Bay). Arrive when the center opens at 12:00 PM (it runs through evening). Start with the Ali'i Luau lunch package or explore the six authentic village recreations — Hawaii, Samoa, Tonga, Fiji, Tahiti, and Aotearoa. Participate in hands-on cultural activities: coconut husking, fire-making, poi pounding, and canoe rides.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring PCC villages throughout the afternoon. Catch the 'Huki' canoe pageant on the lagoon (usually around 2:30 PM) — a colorful, musical parade of traditional canoes representing each island culture. Kids will love the interactive demonstrations and performances.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for the world-famous 'Ha: Breath of Life' evening show — a spectacular 90-minute Polynesian performance with fire dancing, drumming, and storytelling. Dinner is included in most PCC packages (buffet-style Hawaiian feast with kalua pork, poi, lomi salmon, and haupia dessert).

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the boutique stay before departing — toast, fruit, yogurt, or a local café stop
meals.lunch: Included in PCC package (Gateway Buffet or Gateway Bar & Grill on-site, ~$15–20 if not bundled)
meals.dinner: Included in PCC Ali'i Luau or Ambassador package (~$120–160/adult, ~$80–100/child — book the bundle for best value)

day_by_day.notes: Book PCC tickets online in advance — bundle packages (villages + luau + show) offer the best value. The center is run by BYU–Hawaii students; alcohol is not served. Comfortable walking shoes essential. Arrive by noon to maximize time.

day_by_day.morning: Relax morning — sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast. Head to Sandy Beach Park (~5 min from Hanauma Bay) for a family beach morning. Note: Sandy Beach has powerful shore break — best for watching bodyboarders rather than swimming for young children. Alternatively, head to Waimanalo Beach, one of Oahu's most beautiful and calm family-friendly beaches (~15 min drive).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Sea Life Park Hawaii (~10 min from the hotel) — a marine park featuring dolphin and sea lion encounters, penguin exhibits, shark tank, and sea turtle lagoon. Great for kids. Dolphin Royal Swim experiences can be booked in advance (~$60–180/person depending on interaction level).
day_by_day.evening: Low-key dinner back near the hotel — try Assaggio Italian Restaurant in Hawaii Kai for a family-friendly, mid-range Italian meal (~$20–35/person) or pick up fresh poke bowls and sides from Foodland Farms (a local grocery with excellent prepared foods) for a relaxed dinner at the boutique stay.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at the boutique stay or a nearby café — try Kalapawai Market (Kailua area) for fresh pastries and coffee if doing a morning drive
meals.lunch: Casual lunch at Sea Life Park's on-site café, or pack a picnic for the beach (~$10–15/person)
meals.dinner: Assaggio Italian Restaurant, Hawaii Kai (~$20–35/person) or Foodland Farms poke and prepared foods (~$10–20/person)

day_by_day.notes: Sea Life Park dolphin encounters must be booked in advance. Check tide charts for Sandy Beach. Waimanalo Beach is calmer and better for young swimmers. This is a good mid-trip rest day to recharge before inter-island travel.

day_by_day.morning: Inter-island flight to Maui — book an early morning flight from HNL to OGG (Kahului Airport, Maui). Hawaiian Airlines and Southwest offer frequent 35-minute flights (~$60–120/person round-trip if booked in advance). Check out of the boutique stay, store luggage, and head to the airport. Pick up a rental car at OGG — essential for Maui exploration.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to a mid-range hotel in the Kaanapali or Lahaina area (e.g., Aston at Papakea Resort or Hyatt Regency Maui). Spend the afternoon at Kaanapali Beach — consistently rated one of America's best beaches. Swim, snorkel around Black Rock (Pu'u Keka'a), and relax on the wide, calm shoreline.
day_by_day.evening: Luau Dinner at Old Lahaina Luau — one of Hawaii's most authentic and celebrated luau experiences. Enjoy a traditional feast of kalua pig (cooked in an imu underground oven), lomi salmon, haupia, and poi, paired with live Hawaiian music and hula performances. A truly memorable family experience.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at the boutique stay or airport café before the flight
meals.lunch: Grab plate lunches near Lahaina town — try Aloha Mixed Plate on the waterfront (~$12–18/person) for classic Hawaiian comfort food with ocean views
meals.dinner: Old Lahaina Luau (~$130–160/adult, ~$85–95/child — book well in advance, this sells out weeks ahead)

day_by_day.notes: Old Lahaina Luau is extremely popular — book 4–6 weeks in advance minimum. Confirm rental car reservation before flying. Note: parts of Lahaina were affected by the 2023 wildfires; check current access and conditions. The luau venue itself has continued operations.

day_by_day.morning: Road to Hana Scenic Drive — depart early (by 7:00–7:30 AM) from Kaanapali/Lahaina to beat traffic. The 65-mile drive along Maui's northeastern coast features 600+ curves and 59 bridges. First major stop: Twin Falls (~11 miles in) for an easy family hike to beautiful waterfalls. Continue to Ke'anae Peninsula for stunning lava rock coastline views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Road to Hana — stop at Wai'anapanapa State Park (black sand beach and sea caves; reservations required online). Continue to Hana town for a late lunch. Visit the Garden of Eden Arboretum or Oheo Gulch (Seven Sacred Pools) if time and energy allow. Begin the return drive by 3:00–4:00 PM to avoid driving the winding road after dark.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kaanapali/Lahaina area by early evening. Casual dinner to recover from the long day — Lahaina Grill or Mala Ocean Tavern for a relaxed, mid-range meal with fresh local fish (~$25–45/person). Early bedtime recommended after the full-day drive.

meals.breakfast: Pack breakfast items the night before — granola bars, fruit, and coffee in a travel mug for the early start
meals.lunch: Hana Farms stand or Braddah Hutts BBQ in Hana town (~$10–15/person) — cash preferred at roadside stands. Pack extra snacks and water for the road.
meals.dinner: Mala Ocean Tavern, Lahaina (~$25–40/person) or Lahaina Fish Co. for fresh seafood with harbor views (~$25–45/person)

day_by_day.notes: Wai'anapanapa State Park requires advance reservations ($5/person + $10 parking). Download an offline map (Google Maps or Gaia GPS) as cell service is spotty. Bring motion sickness remedies for kids sensitive to winding roads. Pack reef-safe sunscreen, bug spray, and layers. This is a long day — 10–12 hours total.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning after the Road to Hana. Sleep in, enjoy a hotel breakfast, and spend the morning relaxing at Kaanapali Beach. Optional: take a whale-watching cruise (seasonal Aug may have some activity) or a snorkel cruise to Molokini Crater — book through Trilogy Excursions or Pacific Whale Foundation (~$100–130/adult, ~$65–85/child).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Lahaina Historic Town — walk the historic waterfront, visit the 150-year-old Banyan Tree (a must-see), browse local art galleries, and stop at the Lahaina Heritage Museum to learn about the town's whaling history and Hawaiian culture. Great for families and leisurely paced.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset dinner at Kaanapali Beach — many hotels offer beachside dining. Try Leilani's on the Beach at Whaler's Village (~$25–45/person) for fresh fish, cocktails, and spectacular sunset views over the Pacific. Alternatively, enjoy a sunset stroll along Kaanapali's Beachfront Path.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or nearby café — try Gazebo Restaurant in Napili for famous macadamia nut pancakes (expect a wait, arrive early, ~$12–18/person)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Whaler's Village food court or Maui Tacos (~$10–15/person)
meals.dinner: Leilani's on the Beach, Kaanapali (~$25–45/person) — sunset views are spectacular, arrive 30 min before sunset for best seating

day_by_day.notes: Molokini snorkel cruises depart from Maalaea Harbor early morning (~6:30–7:00 AM) — book the day before if interested. The Lahaina Banyan Tree is free to visit and a great photo opportunity. Check if any free Hawaiian music or hula performances are scheduled at Whaler's Village (they often run on weekends).

day_by_day.morning: Drive to the North Shore of Maui — visit Hookipa Beach Park to watch world-class windsurfers and kitesurfers. Continue to Paia town, a charming hippie-surf village with boutique shops, art galleries, and excellent breakfast spots. Explore the town on foot and browse local crafts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Makena Beach (Big Beach) — one of Maui's most beautiful and expansive beaches with golden sand and clear blue water. Swim, bodysurf, or simply relax. Nearby Little Beach (a short hike over the rock) is popular but note it's clothing-optional. Return to the hotel by late afternoon for a final Maui swim at Kaanapali.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Maui dinner — splurge slightly at Merriman's Kapalua (~$40–65/person) for farm-to-table Hawaiian regional cuisine with ocean views, or keep it casual at Star Noodle in Lahaina (~$15–25/person) for creative noodle dishes and small plates. Pack bags tonight for the morning return to Oahu.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast in Paia town — Paia Bay Coffee & Bar or Café des Amis for crepes, bowls, and strong coffee (~$10–15/person)
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic from a Paia grocery/deli for Big Beach, or grab shrimp plates from a food truck near Kihei on the way back (~$12–18/person)
meals.dinner: Star Noodle, Lahaina (~$15–25/person) for a fun, family-friendly atmosphere, or Merriman's Kapalua (~$40–65/person) for a special farewell meal

day_by_day.notes: Big Beach (Makena) can have strong shore break — supervise children closely near the water. The drive from Kaanapali to Makena is about 30–40 min. Return rental car to OGG airport the following morning — confirm drop-off time. Pack and organize bags this evening.

day_by_day.morning: Return inter-island flight from Maui (OGG) back to Honolulu (HNL) — book an early-to-mid morning flight to allow time for a final Oahu experience. Drop off rental car at OGG. Upon landing at HNL, store luggage at the airport or head back toward Waikiki for a final few hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final afternoon in Oahu — spend it at Waikiki Beach for one last swim and walk along the waterfront. Visit the Duke Kahanamoku statue for a photo, browse ABC Stores for last-minute souvenirs, or visit the Honolulu Museum of Art (free first Sundays; otherwise ~$20/adult) if time allows and the family is interested.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner near Waikiki or the airport area before the departing flight — Dukes Waikiki is a classic, lively choice with ocean views and Hawaiian-inspired cuisine (~$25–45/person). Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your international/mainland departure for airport check-in and security.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast near OGG airport or a quick hotel breakfast before checkout — Down to Earth Organic & Natural (Kahului) is a great healthy option (~$8–12/person)
meals.lunch: Light lunch in Waikiki — Eggs 'n Things for a late brunch (~$15–20/person) or a final poke bowl from Ono Seafood or Foodland
meals.dinner: Duke's Waikiki (~$25–45/person) for a festive farewell meal with live Hawaiian music, or airport dining if time is short

day_by_day.notes: Confirm return flight times carefully and plan airport arrival accordingly (HNL international departures recommend arriving 3 hours early). Keep one outfit and essentials in carry-on for the final day. Pick up Hawaiian coffee, macadamia nuts, and local chocolate as gifts at the airport duty-free or ABC Stores. Mahalo for a wonderful trip!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Hawaii Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Hanauma Bay, East Oahu Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay
experiences.description: Explore one of Hawaii's most pristine marine sanctuaries with the whole family. Hanauma Bay offers calm, clear waters teeming with colorful tropical fish and sea turtles, making it perfect for beginner and experienced snorkelers alike. Equipment rentals are available on-site and an educational center teaches visitors about the reef ecosystem before entering the water.

experiences.name: Luau Dinner at Old Lahaina Luau
experiences.description: Immerse your family in authentic Hawaiian culture with a traditional luau featuring a feast of kalua pig, poi, lomi salmon, and haupia dessert. Enjoy live music, hula dancing performances, and fire knife dancing under the stars along the oceanfront. This is a memorable cultural dining experience that kids and adults will talk about for years.

experiences.name: Polynesian Cultural Center Day Trip
experiences.description: Spend a full day exploring six authentic Polynesian village recreations representing Hawaii, Samoa, Aotearoa, Fiji, Tahiti, and Tonga. Families can participate in hands-on cultural activities like spear throwing, coconut husking, and traditional weaving. The evening features an all-you-can-eat buffet and a spectacular live show called 'Ha: Breath of Life'.

experiences.name: Surfing Lessons at Waikiki Beach
experiences.description: Take beginner surfing lessons with certified instructors on the gentle, rolling waves of Waikiki, considered one of the best places in the world to learn to surf. Group lessons are available for all ages including young children, and most participants are standing on the board within the first session. A quintessential Hawaiian family activity with iconic Diamond Head views in the background.

experiences.name: Road to Hana Scenic Drive and Waterfalls
experiences.description: Embark on one of the most scenic drives in the world along Maui's northeastern coastline, stopping at lush rainforest waterfalls, black sand beaches, and bamboo forests. Family highlights include swimming at Wailua Falls, exploring the Pools of Oheo, and tasting fresh banana bread from roadside stands. Pack a picnic and make a full day of this breathtaking adventure through tropical paradise.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival — Flight LH lands at 13:00. No morning activities scheduled. Rest and transfer to Hanauma Bay, East Oahu Boutique Stay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private resort check-in experience with welcome lei greeting and complimentary tropical refreshments. Take a leisurely stroll along the coastline near Hanauma Bay to acclimate and enjoy the stunning ocean views. Unpack and settle into your luxury suite.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on your private lanai or the resort's oceanfront terrace. Enjoy a relaxed welcome dinner at the resort's signature restaurant.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or airport dining
meals.lunch: N/A — in transit; grab a light bite at Honolulu International Airport's premium lounge
meals.dinner: Roy's Hawaii Kai — iconic Hawaii fusion cuisine by celebrity chef Roy Yamaguchi, just minutes from Hanauma Bay; known for misoyaki butterfish and molten chocolate soufflé

day_by_day.notes: Arrange a private luxury transfer from Daniel K. Inouye International Airport to the boutique stay. Ask the concierge to pre-book all upcoming experiences. Early bedtime recommended to overcome jet lag.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay — Arrive early (7:00–8:00 AM) to beat crowds and secure the best conditions. Explore one of Hawaii's most pristine marine sanctuaries with the whole family. Book a private guided snorkeling tour for an exclusive, educational experience with a marine naturalist. Spot sea turtles, tropical fish, and vibrant coral reefs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the boutique stay for a poolside lunch and relaxation. Enjoy a family-friendly Hawaiian cultural activity arranged by the resort — lei-making or ukulele lessons on the property.
day_by_day.evening: Drive along the scenic Kalanianaole Highway for a breathtaking sunset view at Makapu'u Point Lookout, then head to dinner.

meals.breakfast: In-room or resort breakfast — fresh tropical fruit platters, açaí bowls, Kona coffee, and eggs Benedict with kalua pork
meals.lunch: Poolside gourmet lunch at the boutique stay — grilled fresh catch tacos, poke bowls, and fresh-pressed juices
meals.dinner: Koko Head Café (upscale brunch-style dinner) or The Willows in Honolulu — elegant Hawaiian regional cuisine in a lush garden setting

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay requires advance reservations; book online at least 2 days prior. Entry is limited — your concierge should handle this. Apply reef-safe sunscreen only. Best snorkeling is in the morning when visibility is clearest.

day_by_day.morning: Surfing Lessons at Waikiki Beach — Drive 20 minutes west to iconic Waikiki. Take private beginner surfing lessons with certified instructors on the gentle, rolling waves. The whole family can participate; instructors tailor sessions for all ages and skill levels. Enjoy the legendary Waikiki backdrop with Diamond Head in the distance.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Waikiki's upscale shopping at the Royal Hawaiian Center and DFS Galleria. Visit the historic Royal Hawaiian Hotel (the 'Pink Palace') for afternoon tea or shave ice at Waiola Shave Ice — a beloved local institution. Stroll along Kalakaua Avenue.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset catamaran sail along the Waikiki coastline — book a private luxury catamaran for the family with champagne, tropical cocktails, and appetizers as the sun dips below the horizon.

meals.breakfast: Eggs 'n Things on Saratoga Road, Waikiki — legendary Hawaiian breakfast spot; try the macadamia nut pancakes
meals.lunch: La Mer at Halekulani Hotel — one of Honolulu's finest French-Hawaiian restaurants with ocean views (reserve in advance)
meals.dinner: Nobu Honolulu at the Nobu Hotel — world-class Japanese-Peruvian fusion; signature black cod with miso and wagyu beef

day_by_day.notes: Book private surfing lessons through a premium operator like Hans Hedemann Surf School for personalized instruction. The catamaran sunset sail should be booked at least 48 hours in advance through the concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Polynesian Cultural Center Day Trip — Depart early (8:30 AM) for the 45-minute drive to Laie on Oahu's North Shore. Spend a full day exploring six authentic Polynesian village recreations representing Hawaii, Samoa, Aotearoa, Fiji, Tahiti, and Tonga. Upgrade to the Ambassador VIP package for private guided tours, reserved front-row seating, and exclusive dining.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Polynesian Cultural Center — watch traditional canoe pageants on the lagoon, participate in hands-on cultural workshops (fire-making, coconut husking, hula), and enjoy the spectacular 'Ha: Breath of Life' show preview exhibits.
day_by_day.evening: Attend the premier 'Ha: Breath of Life' evening show — a breathtaking theatrical production with fire dancing, Polynesian music, and cultural storytelling. Includes an all-you-can-eat Ali'i Luau buffet with traditional Hawaiian fare.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — avocado toast, smoked salmon, tropical fruit, and Kona coffee before departure
meals.lunch: Gateway Restaurant at the Polynesian Cultural Center — included with Ambassador package; enjoy Hawaiian plate lunches and Polynesian specialties
meals.dinner: Ali'i Luau Dinner at Polynesian Cultural Center — kalua pork, poi, lomi salmon, haupia, and more; included in the evening show package

day_by_day.notes: Book the Ambassador VIP package well in advance as it sells out quickly in summer. This is a full-day excursion — pack reef-safe sunscreen, comfortable walking shoes, and light layers for the evening show. The drive to Laie is scenic along the windward coast.

day_by_day.morning: Private helicopter tour of Oahu — Depart from Honolulu's private aviation terminal for a luxury doors-off helicopter experience over Diamond Head, the Ko'olau Mountains, Hanauma Bay from above, Sacred Falls, and the North Shore's famous surf breaks. A once-in-a-lifetime aerial perspective of the island.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the East Oahu area for a relaxing afternoon at Lanikai Beach — consistently rated one of the world's most beautiful beaches. Enjoy calm, crystal-clear turquoise waters perfect for families. Rent premium beach equipment (kayaks, paddleboards) through the resort concierge.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset paddleboard or kayak to the Mokulua Islands (the 'Mokes') just offshore from Lanikai — a magical golden-hour experience. Return for a relaxed resort evening.

meals.breakfast: Room service luxury breakfast on your private lanai — eggs made to order, fresh-squeezed juices, pastries, and tropical fruits
meals.lunch: Kailua Town lunch at Cinnamon's Restaurant — beloved local spot known for guava chiffon pancakes and creative Hawaiian-inspired brunch dishes
meals.dinner: Olive Tree Cafe in Kahala — acclaimed Mediterranean-inspired restaurant with fresh local fish; beloved by Honolulu's food elite

day_by_day.notes: Book the helicopter tour with Blue Hawaiian Helicopters or Paradise Helicopters for the most premium experience. Early morning flights offer the best visibility and lighting. Lanikai Beach has limited parking — the resort can arrange a private shuttle.

day_by_day.morning: Private Sea Turtle Snorkeling and Marine Wildlife Excursion — Book a private luxury catamaran charter departing from Kailua or Hawaii Kai. Snorkel with Hawaiian green sea turtles (honu) in their natural habitat, spot spinner dolphins, and explore hidden sea caves and coves inaccessible from shore. A professional marine naturalist accompanies the family.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Sea Life Park Hawaii at Makapu'u Point — a family-favorite marine attraction just minutes from the boutique stay. Enjoy dolphin encounters, penguin exhibits, sea lion shows, and a Hawaiian reef tank. Book a premium 'Dolphin Royal Swim' interactive experience for the family.
day_by_day.evening: Relax with a luxury family spa session at the resort or a nearby premier spa — Hawaiian lomi lomi massages, keiki (children's) spa treatments, and ocean-view relaxation lounges.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast buffet — made-to-order omelets, açaí bowls, fresh malasadas (Portuguese donuts), and Kona coffee
meals.lunch: On the catamaran — gourmet picnic lunch prepared by a private chef with fresh poke, artisan sandwiches, tropical fruits, and chilled beverages
meals.dinner: Vintage Cave Honolulu — Oahu's most exclusive and intimate fine dining experience; a 12-course chef's tasting menu in a stunning cave-like setting; advance reservation essential

day_by_day.notes: Vintage Cave Honolulu requires reservations weeks in advance and has a dress code. This is a bucket-list dining experience. The private catamaran charter should be booked through the concierge at least 3 days prior.

day_by_day.morning: Inter-island flight to Maui — Depart early on a short 30-minute flight from Honolulu to Kahului, Maui. Check into a luxury resort in Wailea (south Maui) — consider the Four Seasons Resort Maui or Andaz Maui at Wailea for a day-use premium experience. Explore the beautiful Wailea Beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Road to Hana Scenic Drive and Waterfalls — Begin the legendary Road to Hana along Maui's northeastern coastline. Stop at Twin Falls for a refreshing swim, Wai'anapanapa State Park's dramatic black sand beach, and the lush Ke'anae Peninsula. Admire cascading waterfalls and dramatic sea cliffs. Hire a private driver-guide for a stress-free, narrated experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return from Hana at a leisurely pace, stopping for the sunset at a scenic overlook. Check into Wailea luxury resort for the night.

meals.breakfast: Early grab-and-go breakfast at the resort before departure — fresh pastries, fruit, and Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Roadside stops on the Road to Hana — fresh banana bread from the iconic Aunt Sandy's stand, coconut candy, and tropical fruit from local farm stands
meals.dinner: Mama's Fish House in Paia — Maui's most celebrated restaurant; legendary fresh fish caught by named local fishermen; book months in advance

day_by_day.notes: The Road to Hana is a full-day commitment (8–10 hours). Hiring a private driver-guide is highly recommended so the whole family can enjoy the scenery without the stress of navigating 600+ curves. Book Mama's Fish House well in advance — it's one of Hawaii's hardest reservations to get.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise at Haleakalā Summit — Wake at 3:00 AM for the drive up to Haleakalā National Park's 10,023-foot summit to witness one of the world's most spectacular sunrises above the clouds. The ethereal landscape and colors are unforgettable. Dress in warm layers as temperatures near the summit can be in the 40s°F.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Wailea for beach relaxation at the resort's private beach club. Enjoy premium water sports — private surfing lesson, stand-up paddleboarding, or outrigger canoe experience on Wailea Beach. Younger family members can enjoy the resort's luxury kids' club.
day_by_day.evening: Luau Dinner at Old Lahaina Luau — Drive to historic Lahaina town for an authentic Hawaiian luau experience. Immerse the family in traditional Hawaiian culture with a feast of kalua pig, poi, lomi salmon, and fresh fish. Enjoy hula performances, fire knife dancing, and live Hawaiian music under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Light snacks and hot beverages at the Haleakalā Visitor Center (pack a thermos of coffee and granola bars from the resort)
meals.lunch: Monkeypod Kitchen in Wailea — farm-to-table Hawaiian cuisine; excellent fresh fish tacos, craft cocktails, and house-made pies
meals.dinner: Old Lahaina Luau — traditional Hawaiian feast included with luau package; kalua pork, poi, haupia, fresh fish, and tropical desserts

day_by_day.notes: Haleakalā sunrise requires advance reservations through Recreation.gov — the concierge should handle this immediately as spots fill months in advance. Warm layers are essential. The drive from Wailea to the summit takes approximately 1.5–2 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Molokini Crater Snorkeling — Depart from Ma'alaea Harbor on a private luxury catamaran charter to Molokini Crater, a partially submerged volcanic crater 3 miles offshore. Snorkel in the crystal-clear, calm waters of this protected marine sanctuary with visibility up to 150 feet. Spot hundreds of endemic Hawaiian fish species and vibrant coral formations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Whale watching cruise (seasonal — August may offer sightings of late-season humpbacks or year-round spinner dolphins). Return to the resort for a relaxing afternoon at the spa — enjoy a traditional Hawaiian lomi lomi massage and hot stone therapy. Children can enjoy the resort's premium kids' club with supervised Hawaiian cultural activities.
day_by_day.evening: Return inter-island flight from Maui back to Honolulu. Private transfer to the Hanauma Bay boutique stay. Relaxed evening at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast before departure to the harbor — fresh tropical fruit, eggs Benedict, and Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet lunch aboard the private catamaran — fresh sashimi, artisan sandwiches, tropical fruit, and chilled champagne
meals.dinner: Humuhumunukunukuapua'a Restaurant at Grand Wailea (before evening flight) — fine dining in a stunning over-water setting; named after Hawaii's state fish; fresh local catch and prime steaks

day_by_day.notes: Book the Molokini snorkeling charter with a premium operator like Trilogy Excursions for the most luxurious experience with gourmet catering. Confirm the inter-island flight time and allow ample time for the harbor-to-airport transfer.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at Hanauma Bay — Return to Hanauma Bay for one last snorkeling session and a leisurely beach morning. Collect shells, take family photos, and soak in the beauty of this paradise you've called home for 10 days. A private beach picnic breakfast can be arranged by the resort concierge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Luxury shopping and souvenir experience in Honolulu — Visit the Ala Moana Center (the world's largest open-air shopping mall) for high-end boutiques, local Hawaiian designers, and premium souvenir shopping. Stop at Manaola (luxury Hawaiian fashion), Nohea Gallery (fine Hawaiian art and jewelry), and Longs Drugs for classic local treats to bring home.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell sunset dinner at a premier Honolulu restaurant. Private luxury transfer to Daniel K. Inouye International Airport for departure. Mahalo and aloha!

meals.breakfast: Private beach picnic breakfast arranged by the resort — fresh fruit, pastries, smoked salmon, sparkling juice, and Kona coffee at Hanauma Bay
meals.lunch: Mariposa at Neiman Marcus, Ala Moana — elegant upscale dining with panoramic views; popovers with strawberry butter, fresh fish, and premium salads
meals.dinner: Orchids at Halekulani Hotel — one of Honolulu's most romantic and acclaimed restaurants; oceanfront setting, impeccable service, and exquisite Hawaiian regional cuisine; perfect farewell dinner

day_by_day.notes: Pack and check out of the boutique stay before the morning beach excursion — arrange luggage storage with the resort. Confirm departure flight details and allow at least 3 hours before international departure for check-in and security. Ask the resort to prepare a farewell gift bag with local treats for the journey home.
